title: Talking to Boards and Executives About AI
subtitle: Honest timelines, named killcriteria, no 18-month vapor

audioChapters.label: Opening — the board doesn't want vapor

blocks.md: Most VPs lose the board on AI by promising too much. The board doesn't punish honest tradeoffs; it punishes vapor that misses by 18 months. By the end of this lesson you'll know the three sentences a board wants to hear, and the two they never want to hear again.

blocks.caption: What happens when promises outpace pre-committed measurable outcomes.

blocks.title: Mental model: the assumption ledger
blocks.md:
A board ask is a forecast. A forecast without an assumption ledger is a wish. Your job is to write down: *what specifically must be true for this to work, by when will we know, what's the rollback if it doesn't.*

Boards don't punish honest assumption ledgers; they punish surprises.

blocks.caption: Two boardroom slides: the vapor version vs. the dated-commitment version, watched 18 months later.

hi-IN.title: AI-first PowerPoint ka khel
hi-IN.md: Founder ne board mein bola *"hum AI-first hain."* Slide pe 4 ChatGPT screenshots. Investor ne pucha *"specifically kya badla?"* — silence. **AI-first matlab kuch nahi hota agar metric pe nahi dikha.** Vapor ka brand color violet hai.

en.title: Buzzwords, briefly
en.md: Boards have heard 'AI-first' enough times that the phrase now triggers skepticism, not enthusiasm. Replace it with 'we will know by Date Y whether bet X moved metric Z.' Different reaction.

blocks.md:
Every AI bet has four numbers worth declaring up-front:

1. **Investment** — actual rupees and people across 90 days.
2. **Expected outcome** — a specific metric delta, with a date.
3. **Confidence** — your own probability estimate (40%? 70%?).
4. **Cost of being wrong** — what you lose if the bet fails.

A board can debate any of these. They cannot debate vibes.

blocks.caption: The board memo on a postcard. Anything missing here is a missing decision.

blocks.title: Translation moment: 'we want to use AI to reduce CAC'

steps.label: 1. Frame the bet
steps.body: Specific outcome with a date. Not 'reduce CAC'; 'reduce paid CAC by ≥10% by Sep 30, with no LTV regression'.

steps.label: 3. Confidence note
steps.body: Your honest probability. 'We think 50-60%; here's why.'

steps.label: 4. Kill criterion
steps.body: By when, and on what number. 'If at day 45 CAC hasn't moved ≥3%, we kill this and reallocate.'

steps.label: 5. The rollback
steps.body: What happens if it fails. Capital and people freed up; what do they do next.

blocks.prompt: What's the most important sentence in a board AI memo?

choices.label: By Date Y, we will know whether metric Z moved by ≥X%; if not, we kill it.
choices.explain: Correct. A board can govern a dated kill criterion. They cannot govern hope.

choices.label: AI is going to revolutionize everything we do.
choices.explain: This is what every board has heard for 24 months. They want specifics now.

choices.label: Our competitors are all using AI.
choices.explain: FOMO is not a strategy. Boards know this.

choices.label: We've allocated ₹4 crore to AI initiatives.
choices.explain: Numbers without outcomes are budget asks, not strategy.

hi-IN.title: Vichaar samay — the assumption ledger
hi-IN.md: Indian boards mein 'AI strategy' ka literal translation hai *"hum sab kuch karenge, kab pata nahi."* Translate it to: *"yeh number, yeh date, yeh kill criterion."* Ek saans mein bol sako toh better.

en.title: The one-breath test
en.md: If your AI commitment doesn't fit in a one-breath sentence — 'X by Y, killing if Z' — you don't have a commitment. You have an intention.

blocks.md:
Boards trust executives who plan for failure. The rollback narrative — what happens if this bet fails, who absorbs the cost, what gets reallocated — is the single most underrated trust-building move with a board.

Most VPs hide the rollback because they think it signals weakness. It doesn't. *Hiding* it signals weakness. *Pre-committing* to it signals competence.

blocks.alt: A diagram with two paths from day 0: 'success path' and 'rollback path'. Both paths have specific actions named.
blocks.caption: Pre-commit both paths. The board reviews both. Failure is not a surprise; it's a contingency.

coach.name: Board-Member Bharat
coach.role: Independent director, 14 board seats over 20 years

intro: Tell me whether each VP is being **honest**, **vague**, or **selling**.
I've sat through 800+ AI memos. Pick carefully.

scenarios.situation: VP says: 'AI will transform our customer support entirely. We expect significant improvements.'
scenarios.explain: Vague. No metric, no date, no kill criterion. Board cannot govern this.

scenarios.situation: VP says: 'By Sep 30 we will reduce ticket-handling cost by ≥18%, measured against this quarter's baseline. Confidence 55%. If at day 45 we don't see ≥6% movement, we stop and reallocate the 2 engineers.'
scenarios.explain: Honest. Three numbers, a date, a kill criterion, a probability. This is a memo a board can govern.

scenarios.situation: VP says: 'We're investing ₹4 crore in AI to maintain competitive parity. The market expects this of us.'
scenarios.explain: Selling — using FOMO and 'market expectation' as a substitute for outcome. Board will see through this. Red flag.

scenarios.situation: VP says: 'We've identified 3 AI bets. Each has its own outcome, kill date, and rollback. Combined investment is ₹3.6 crore. Worst case, we're out 1 quarter and 6 engineers.'
scenarios.explain: Honest. Portfolio framing with explicit downside. Board likes this.

scenarios.situation: VP says: 'AI is the future. We need to act now or we'll be left behind.'
scenarios.explain: Pure FOMO sales pitch. Board has heard this 47 times. Always flag.

blocks.title: The classic trap: hiding the rollback
blocks.md:
Most VPs think hiding the failure case makes the pitch stronger. It doesn't.

**Pre-committing the rollback is the single highest-trust move available with a board.** It tells them: *I've thought about how this fails. I'm not going to surprise you in 6 months.*

The pitches that lose boards are the ones where the executive shows up at month 5 with a panicked memo asking for more time. The pitches that win are the ones where the kill criterion was on slide 3.

items.detail: First. Without this, the rest is fiction.

items.label: The expected outcome (specific number, specific date)
The narrative (why this bet vs alternatives)

blocks.instruction: Write the one-breath sentence for an AI bet you've considered. Format: 'By [date], we will know whether [metric] moved by [Δ]; if not, we [kill action].' Be specific about ALL four placeholders.
blocks.expected: By Sep 30 2026, we will know whether paid CAC moved by ≥10%; if not, we kill the bet and reallocate the 4 engineers to our retention work — and we'll do a public post-mortem within 14 days of the kill.

blocks.prompt: Pick the TWO statements about board AI communication that are TRUE:

choices.label: Pre-committing a rollback signals competence, not weakness
choices.explain: Correct. Boards trust executives who plan for failure.

choices.label: A confidence note (e.g. '55% likely') is more useful than a single optimistic forecast
choices.explain: Correct. Honest probability lets the board calibrate.

choices.label: The bigger the AI promise, the more the board will fund
choices.explain: False. Sophisticated boards now distrust large AI promises after 24 months of overpromising.

choices.label: If you don't know your kill criterion, list it as 'TBD'
choices.explain: False. 'TBD' on a kill criterion = no kill criterion. Decide before pitching.

hi-IN.title: Mahaul ka management — Indian board edition
hi-IN.md: Indian boards mein technical questions kam aate hain; *"why this, why now, what if it fails?"* zyada aate hain. Tu agar pehle se yeh teen sawal handle kar le, baaki natural follow-through hai.

en.title: What Indian boards actually ask
en.md: Most Indian board AI questions are not technical — they're 'why this, why now, what if it fails.' Pre-answer all three, in that order, in your memo.

points: Board AI memos need four lines: investment, expected outcome, confidence, kill criterion
The rollback narrative is the highest-trust move you can make with a board
'AI-first' / 'transformation' / 'parity' are board allergens — replace with dated commitments
Pre-commit your kill criterion on slide 3, not when the metric flatlines at month 5
One-breath sentence test: 'X by Y, killing if Z'

blocks.prompt: Write the kill criterion for one AI bet on your current roadmap. If you can't, you don't have a roadmap — you have a wishlist.
